stories.title: Sephora Relocates Meatpacking District Store with Long-Term Lease
stories.excerpt: Taconic Partners and Nuveen Real Estate signed a long-term lease with Sephora for approximately 4,200 square feet of ground-floor retail space at 401 W. 14th St. in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District. The current Meatpacking location on Ninth Avenue will be relocated to the new store, which is expected to open in the first quarter of 2027. Positioned adjacent to Apple’s Meatpacking District flagship, the location is at the center of one of Manhattan’s most prominent retail corners. “Sephora is a leading prestige beauty retailer and their move to 401 W. 14th St. underscores the importance that a highly visible and trafficked location has on the establishment of a strong retail presence.” said Michael Adelstein, VP, Taconic Partners. “The Meatpacking District, and in particular the corner of Ninth Avenue and 14th Street, is one of the most iconic and in-demand shopping destinations in the world.” Jason Greenstone of Cushman & Wakefield represented Taconic. Virginia Pittarelli of Retail by MONA represented Sephora. The post Sephora Relocates Meatpacking District Store with Long-Term Lease appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sephora relocates Meatpacking District NYC store to 4,200 SF at 401 W. 14th St., opening Q1 2027.
Taconic Partners and Nuveen Real Estate signed long-term lease adjacent to Apple flagship retail.
Meatpacking District remains Manhattan's highest-traffic retail destination, driving prestige brand consolidation.
stories.summary: Sephora is relocating its Ninth Avenue Meatpacking store to a new 4,200-square-foot ground-floor space at 401 W. 14th Street, positioned directly adjacent to Apple's flagship, with opening expected in Q1 2027. Taconic Partners and Nuveen Real Estate signed the long-term lease with the beauty retailer. The move underscores the Meatpacking District's status as one of Manhattan's most iconic and in-demand retail destinations.
stories.impact: Manhattan's Meatpacking District continues consolidating premium retail and office anchors (Apple, now Sephora expansion), signaling sustained foot traffic and rental resilience in the submarket. This strengthens the case for mixed-use residential development in adjacent blocks—retail density and brand presence drive renter demand and commanding rents in the surrounding neighborhoods.

stories.title: Avatar Furnishes Bridge Loan on Fully Leased Santa Ana Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Avatar Financial Group LLC provided a $4.75-million bridge loan secured by a fully leased warehouse and distribution building in Santa Ana. The two-year, first-lien loan was originated at approximately 60% loan-to-value. The financing replaced two loans with one, retiring the property’s existing first mortgage along with a junior loan that had passed its maturity date. The tenant had invested substantially in its own build-out, and rent had commenced before the loan closed. After approximately 6 months of rental income, the sponsor intends to obtain long-term financing and repay Avatar’s bridge loan. “A lease that has just commenced doesn’t underwrite the same as one with a payment history behind it,” said T.R. Hazelrigg IV, Avatar’s president and co-founder. “A bank waits for that history to exist. Our job is deciding whether it will. At a 60% basis, with the tenant’s own money already in the space, that wasn’t a hard call.” The 18,876-square-foot light industrial facility at 4001 W. Carriage Dr. sits on approximately 0.9 acres, less than two miles from Interstate 405 and State Route 55. The post Avatar Furnishes Bridge Loan on Fully Leased Santa Ana Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Avatar Financial provided $4.75M bridge loan on fully leased Santa Ana warehouse at 60% LTV.
18,876 SF light industrial property at 4001 W. Carriage Dr., less than 2 miles from I-405/SR-55.
Bridge filled gap between lease commencement and seasoning required for permanent financing.
stories.summary: Avatar Financial Group originated a $4.75-million, two-year bridge loan secured by a fully leased 18,876-square-foot warehouse and distribution building in Santa Ana. The first-lien loan was structured at approximately 60% LTV and replaced two existing loans. The tenant had already invested substantially in build-out and commenced rent before closing; the sponsor intends to obtain long-term financing within six months.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. This is industrial/logistics real estate financing, a separate capital and tenant ecosystem. No signals on residential demand, labor migration, or competing capital flows that would materially affect apartment underwriting in Orange County or Southern California.

stories.title: George Comfort & Sons Refinances 200 Madison for $386M
stories.excerpt: George Comfort & Sons, and its partners Loeb Partners Realty and Jamestown, completed a $386-million refinancing of 200 Madison Ave., a 750,000-square-foot Grand Central district office tower. New York Life provided the five-year floating rate loan, structured with a three-year initial term and two 12-month extension options. Proceeds will be used to pay off 200 Madison’s existing debt and fund ongoing leasing. The refi follows an August agreement with Havas Health for a 15-year extension and headquarters expansion, which grew the global firm’s footprint to 254,118 square feet. “This refinancing underscores the lending community’s confidence in office assets like 200 Madison Ave. that are defined by top-tier amenities, unrivaled location and strong sponsorship,” said George Comfort & Sons president and CEO Peter S. Duncan. Jonathan Estreich, Peter A. Duncan and Egor Petrov of Estreich & Company and Adam Spies, Adam Doneger and Willis Robbins of Newmark assisted in arranging the transaction. The post George Comfort & Sons Refinances 200 Madison for $386M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: George Comfort & Sons refinanced 200 Madison Ave. (750K SF office tower) for $386M with New York Life.
Five-year floating-rate loan follows Havas Health 15-year extension and 254K SF expansion in Grand Central.
Strong sponsorship and top-tier amenities enabled financing despite office sector headwinds.
stories.summary: George Comfort & Sons, Loeb Partners Realty, and Jamestown completed a $386-million refinancing of 200 Madison Avenue, a 750,000-square-foot Grand Central office tower. New York Life provided the five-year floating-rate loan with a three-year initial term and two one-year extension options. The refi follows an August agreement with Havas Health for a 15-year extension and headquarters expansion to 254,118 square feet.
stories.impact: Office capital remaining available for prime Manhattan assets with best-in-class sponsorship and amenities signals uneven office recovery. Grand Central submarket office strength (Havas expansion, refi confidence) supports residential demand in adjacent neighborhoods—office workers spending time in upgraded workspaces and dining/retail clusters drive multifamily demand in the surrounding East Midtown and Flatiron submarkets.

stories.title: Zurich Affiliate Acquires San Francisco Offices with Leasing Upside
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has arranged the sale of 410 Townsend, a historic 78,455-square-foot office building in downtown San Francisco. An affiliate of Zurich Alternative Asset Management purchased the building for $47.4 million from New York Life Real Estate Investors and Bridgeton Holdings. Seth Siegel and Ryan Venezia of Cushman & Wakefield’s Northern California Capital Markets Team led the transaction. “410 Townsend is a compelling example of San Francisco’s rapid rebound and the opportunity to capitalize on the market’s strengthening fundamentals; this is the first ‘round trip’ for a San Francisco office building,” said Siegel. “Transactions like this demonstrate that investors are taking a closer look at San Francisco assets where the right combination of location, quality and basis can create meaningful opportunities.” Built in 1912, 410 Townsend features exposed brick and heavy timber construction while offering a range of modern amenities and flexible office layouts. With its current 65% occupancy, the property provides significant potential for additional leasing and value creation. The post Zurich Affiliate Acquires San Francisco Offices with Leasing Upside appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Zurich Alternative Asset Management acquired 410 Townsend, San Francisco 78K SF office building, for $47.4M.
Property at 65% occupancy; first 'round trip' office sale signals investor confidence in SF rebound.
Historic 1912 building with modern amenities near downtown SF core.
stories.summary: An affiliate of Zurich Alternative Asset Management purchased 410 Townsend, a historic 78,455-square-foot office building in downtown San Francisco, for $47.4 million from New York Life Real Estate Investors and Bridgeton Holdings. The 1912-built property features exposed brick and heavy timber with modern amenities and currently sits at 65% occupancy, providing meaningful leasing upside. The sale marks the first 'round trip' for a San Francisco office building, demonstrating investor appetite for assets with the right location, quality, and basis.
stories.impact: San Francisco office market stabilizing with opportunistic capital returning and leasing-based upside plays. Returning investor confidence in downtown SF office signals job market and foot traffic recovery, which strengthens residential demand in adjacent South of Market, Mission, and downtown residential corridors. Multifamily developers should monitor office absorption and tenant demand—office recovery precedes apartment rent growth in transit-rich urban cores.

stories.title: JLL Arranges JV Equity, Acquisition Debt on Jersey City Multifamily
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged joint venture equity and acquisition financing for Jasmin Terrace II, a 56-unit, newly built, luxury apartment building in Jersey City. Senior managing directors Thomas R. Didio and Thomas E. Didio Jr., senior director Gerard Quinn, associate Michael Mataras and senior analyst Joseph Gruber worked on behalf of the borrower, Tower Management Service LP, to arrange a joint venture equity investment from Lakerock, forming a new partnership between the two firms. JLL then represented the partnership in securing the $16.5-million, five-year, fixed-rate acquisition loan through RWC Lending. Tower is making its debut in the Jersey City market. Delivered in 2024, Jasmin Terrace II is located at 412 Whiton St. in the Bergen-Lafayette neighborhood of Jersey City.  The property benefits from walkable access to Jersey City’s light rail network connecting to PATH trains and the ferry, proximity to Liberty State Park and a rapidly maturing retail and dining scene. The post JLL Arranges JV Equity, Acquisition Debt on Jersey City Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL arranged $16.5M acquisition loan and JV equity for Jasmin Terrace II, 56-unit luxury Jersey City, delivered 2024.
Tower Management Service LP (debut in Jersey City) partnered with Lakerock; RWC Lending provided fixed-rate loan.
Bergen-Lafayette location offers light rail/PATH/ferry access, Liberty State Park proximity, maturing retail.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged joint venture equity from Lakerock and a $16.5-million, five-year, fixed-rate acquisition loan through RWC Lending for Jasmin Terrace II, a 56-unit newly built luxury apartment building in Jersey City's Bergen-Lafayette neighborhood. Tower Management Service LP, making its debut in Jersey City, partnered with Lakerock to form the JV. The property, delivered in 2024 at 412 Whiton Street, benefits from walkable access to light rail, PATH trains, ferry service, and Liberty State Park proximity.
stories.impact: Fixed-rate acquisition financing available for newly delivered luxury multifamily in Jersey City signals continued capital confidence in Bergen-Lafayette and PATH-accessible Hudson County markets. Strong transit connectivity, retail maturation, and developer interest in the submarket (Tower Management's entry) indicate sustained demand from Manhattan-proximate renters. Monitor Jersey City's light rail activation and retail pace—conversion of industrial/warehouse space to mixed-use and dining will accelerate rental absorption and support future development starts in the waterfront and neighborhood cores.

stories.title: Virginia, Maryland Tighten Data Center Rules as Scrutiny Intensifies
stories.excerpt: Data center development will face tighter regulations across the Mid-Atlantic after officials in Virginia and Maryland unveiled new frameworks to corral the intense growth. Maryland Gov. Wes Moore on Wednesday announced an executive order establishing a review process for data centers of 25 megawatts or more whenever developers seek state permits, incentives or letters of support. The order also creates a task force that will evaluate projects based on their effects on ratepayers and the grid. The governor said local officials will still decide whether projects can ultimately move forward. Projects that do not align with the new framework can face deferred state review and will not be eligible for state advocacy or certain incentives. Moore also said his administration will seek to repeal Maryland’s sales and use tax exemption that was enacted in 2020. That followed a day after the Prince William County Board of County Supervisors in Virginia unanimously approved changes that largely end by-right data center development. The county — which is one of the country’s largest data center markets — is set to shrink its Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District from 9,698 acres to roughly 3,641 acres, and new proposals outside the overlay must proceed through a special-use permit process. Prince William created the overlay in 2016 to encourage data center development near high-voltage transmission lines. Prince William’s own planning documents describe the zoning amendment as a structural shift from the previous approach in how the county approves new data centers. And, last week, Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger announced a broad “Data Center Accountability Framework” and signed Executive Order 22, immediately directing state agencies to increase transparency, environmental oversight and scrutiny of the data center industry. Separately, her administration is proposing legislation for the 2027 legislative session that would eliminate by-right approval for data centers
bullets: Maryland Gov. Moore issued executive order requiring data center review for 25+ megawatt projects; task force to evaluate grid impact.
Prince William County, Virginia unanimously approved tighter data center regulations, largely ending by-right development.
Maryland targeting repeal of 2020 sales/use tax exemption for data centers.
stories.summary: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore announced an executive order establishing a review process for data centers of 25 megawatts or more, creating a task force to evaluate projects based on effects on ratepayers and the grid. Local officials retain final approval authority. Moore also signaled intention to repeal Maryland's 2020 sales and use tax exemption for data centers. One day prior, Prince William County, Virginia unanimously approved regulatory changes largely ending by-right data center development.
stories.impact: Tightening data center regulations in Virginia and Maryland will slow hyperscale facility development and associated corporate ancillary demand (cloud, AI, software firms seeking co-location). Mid-Atlantic metros (Northern Virginia, greater Baltimore) that benefited from data center spillover job creation and corporate relocation will face softer white-collar employment growth forecasts. Multifamily developers should reduce near-term demand assumptions in NoVA and Maryland submarkets; long-term office-to-residential conversion becomes more feasible as corporate footprint growth moderates.

stories.title: Hudson Bay Capital Refis Microsoft-Anchored SoHo Building With $85M Loan
stories.excerpt: InterVest Capital Partners has sealed an $85 million loan to refinance an mixed-use office and retail property leased largely to Microsoft in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. Hudson Bay Capital provided the loan for the seven-story building at 300 Lafayette Street. Microsoft occupies the entire 63,000-square-foot office component of the 2019-–built property on floors two through seven. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Jordan Roeschlaub, Nick Scribani, John Caraviello and Ryan Bub. “300 Lafayette Street is as good as boutique product gets in Lower Manhattan,” Scribani said in a statement. “Lender interest was deep and competitive.” The property has 19,028 square feet of retail space on the ground floor and lower level leased to Neko Health, New Era and Goldwin. The COOKFOX-designed building inked a long-term lease with Microsoft for the office portion in March 2019, just before construction was completed, CO first reported at the time. “Buildings like this are nearly impossible to replicate at today’s replacement costs,.” Rob Rothschild, managing director and head of real estate at InterVest Capital Partners, said in a statement. “This financing reflects the strength of the property and its tenancy.” Hudson Bay Capital declined to comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: InterVest Capital Partners refinanced Microsoft-anchored 300 Lafayette Street SoHo mixed-use for $85M with Hudson Bay Capital.
Microsoft occupies 63K SF office (floors 2–7) on long-term lease; 19K SF retail (Neko Health, New Era, Goldwin).
2019-built COOKFOX-designed building achieved strong lender appetite despite NYC office sector uncertainty.
stories.summary: InterVest Capital Partners secured an $85 million refinancing loan from Hudson Bay Capital for 300 Lafayette Street, a mixed-use office and retail property in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. Microsoft occupies the entire 63,000-square-foot office component (floors two through seven) under a long-term lease inked in March 2019. The ground floor and lower level contain 19,028 square feet of retail space leased to Neko Health, New Era, and Goldwin. Newmark negotiated the debt with strong lender interest.
stories.impact: Microsoft's long-term SoHo anchor and deep lender confidence in Lower Manhattan mixed-use signifies sustained corporate office demand in high-amenity neighborhoods. SoHo's retail-office activation and tech tenant concentration support residential demand in adjacent neighborhoods and blocks. Developers should prioritize mixed-use projects in SoHo, Noho, and Greenwich Village with ground-floor retail and proximate residential—office tenants (tech, media, design) drive foot traffic, evening economy, and rental demand in these neighborhoods.

stories.title: Nomic AI Inks 5K-SF Deal at 99 University Place Near Union Square
stories.excerpt: Four tenants have signed office deals adding up to 15,593 square feet at a 10-story office building near Manhattan’s Union Square, Commercial Observer has learned. Design software firm Nomic AI, therapy space provider Therapeutic Alliance Suites and construction systems developer T Moriarty & Son each signed 4,890-square-foot leases across full floors of Bijan Nassi’s 99 University Place, according to landlord broker Noah & Co. Asking rent in the building is $55 per square foot, Noah & Co. said. “The velocity at 99 University speaks to the demand we’re seeing for the relatively limited supply of true office buildings remaining in Greenwich Village,” Benjamin Blumenthal of Noah & Co., who represented the landlord alongside Rachel Fox, said in a statement. “There are only so many buildings in the neighborhood that combine a great location with authentic character, high ceilings, natural light and manageable full-floor footprints. When those spaces are positioned properly and brought to the market with real attention, tenants respond quickly.” Eddie Sisca and Taylor Walker of CBRE negotiated on behalf of Nomic AI in its lease for the entire 10th floor. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Drew Silvester of Colliers, who represented Therapeutic Alliance Suites in its sixth-floor transaction, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Todd Korren and Noah Caspi of Lee & Associates NYC handled the transaction for T Moriarty & Son in its negotiations for the ​​fifth-floor space. Lee & Associates did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The smallest of the four leases was for alternative asset management firm BSQ Capital Partners, which will occupy a 923-square-foot space on the property’s second floor. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nomic AI, Therapeutic Alliance Suites, T Moriarty & Son signed four 4,890 SF full-floor leases at 99 University Place.
Union Square office building at $55/SF asking rent; strong velocity signaling limited supply of quality boutique stock.
Deals total 15,593 SF across tech, wellness, and construction systems tenants.
stories.summary: Four tenants signed office deals totaling 15,593 square feet at 99 University Place, a 10-story building near Manhattan's Union Square. Design software firm Nomic AI, therapy space provider Therapeutic Alliance Suites, and construction systems developer T Moriarty & Son each signed 4,890-square-foot full-floor leases at $55 per square foot asking rent. Landlord broker Noah & Co. highlighted strong tenant velocity reflecting demand for the limited supply of authentic office buildings with high ceilings, natural light, and manageable floor plates.
stories.impact: Continued strong leasing velocity for boutique, character-driven office near Union Square signals sustained demand from tech, wellness, and creative tenants in Greenwich Village. Multifamily developers should view this as reinforcing renter demand in adjacent East Village, Flatiron, and NoHo—younger, educated office tenants in software, therapy, and design sectors are premium multifamily renters. Limited office supply and full-floor takeup indicate tight office markets that support adjacent residential absorption and pricing power.

stories.title: Wells Fargo Supplies $456M Refi for Family Dollar’s Distribution Center Portfolio
stories.excerpt: The owners of Family Dollar have secured $455.7 million to refinance existing loans on its 7.1 million-square-foot portfolio of leased distribution centers, Commercial Observer has learned. Wells Fargo provided the floating-rate loan to 1959 RE Holdings, the entity controlled and partially owned by private equity firms Brigade Capital Management and Macellum Capital Management. The refinancing will support Family Dollar’s ongoing operational improvements following Brigade and Macellum’s acquisition of the retailer from Dollar Tree in 2025. The portfolio spans eight properties in Utah, New York, Oklahoma, Indiana, Iowa, Virginia, Kentucky and Florida, and currently serves approximately 7,100 Family Dollar retail stores nationwide. A JLL Capital Markets team of Christopher Peck, Christopher Pratt and Alex Staikos arranged the financing. “The transaction attracted significant lender interest because it sits at the intersection of a successful private equity-led turnaround of a longstanding, recession-proof operating business and mission-critical industrial real estate at an attractive basis,” Peck said in a statement. The bulk distribution centers have hosted the retailer’s operations for an average of 22.2 years. Locations include 907,000-square-foot facilities at 3949 Family Dollar Parkway in the South Florida city of Marianna, and 155 Fairground Road in Front Royal, Va. Spokespeople for Wells Fargo, Brigade and Macellum did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Wells Fargo provided $455.7M floating-rate refi on Family Dollar's 7.1M SF distribution center portfolio across 8 states.
Brigade Capital Management and Macellum Capital Management (post-2025 DTI acquisition) control 1959 RE Holdings.
Portfolio serves ~7,100 Family Dollar stores; facilities span Utah, New York, Oklahoma, Indiana, Iowa, Virginia, Kentucky, Florida.
stories.summary: The owners of Family Dollar secured $455.7 million in floating-rate refinancing from Wells Fargo for their 7.1-million-square-foot portfolio of leased distribution centers. The loan went to 1959 RE Holdings, controlled and partially owned by Brigade Capital Management and Macellum Capital Management, which acquired Family Dollar from Dollar Tree in 2025. The portfolio spans eight properties across Utah, New York, Oklahoma, Indiana, Iowa, Virginia, Kentucky, and Florida and currently serves approximately 7,100 Family Dollar retail stores nationwide.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Family Dollar's DC portfolio refinancing reflects private equity-led retail turnaround and supply-chain resilience, not residential demand. However, continued investment in retail logistics and small-format retail footprint expansion (7,100 stores) may signal ongoing demand for workforce housing near distribution and retail hubs in secondary and tertiary markets—monitor wage/population inflows in those regions for complementary residential opportunity.

stories.title: Conduct AI Takes 7K SF at Capstone’s 140 Crosby Street for First U.S. Office
stories.excerpt: A London-based artificial intelligence firm developing enterprise software is establishing its first U.S. office presence in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. The rapidly growing Conduct AI has signed a 6,705-square-foot lease on the entire third floor of 140 Crosby Street, owned by Capstone Equities, Rugby Realty and Republic Investment Company, according to landlord broker JLL. JLL did not immediately disclose the length of the lease or the rent involved. The asking rents at the building, which the landlord acquired in May for $51.4 million from an entity tied to Madison Capital, range between $150 to $165 per square foot, JLL said. “Signing a fast-growing company like Conduct AI as our first new tenant speaks to the appeal of 140 Crosby and the kind of companies this property attracts,” Daven Roshan, director of acquisitions for Capstone Equities, said in a statement. “With committed new ownership, a clear plan for the property and a strong partnership with JLL, we’re bringing a focused leasing and marketing strategy to a building that offers tenants a modern, purpose-built office at a scale that still feels intimate and distinctly SoHo.” JLL’s Clark Finney, Alex Riguardi and Dana Goldman represented the landlord in the transaction, while Max Mond and John Brennan of Savills negotiated on behalf of the tenant. Founded in 2024, Conduct raised $60 million in its Series A funding round in June and will accommodate more than 60 employees at its new SoHo office. “Conduct approached this search with a clear objective: a workplace that reflects the caliber of its team and supports its next phase of growth,” Mond said in a statement. “Capstone’s vision for 140 Crosby and the way they have positioned the building set it apart from every comparable asset we evaluated in the submarket. bullets: Conduct AI (London-based AI software firm) signed 6,705 SF lease for entire third floor at 140 Crosby Street SoHo.
First U.S. office for fast-growing AI enterprise software company; building asking rents $150–$165/SF.
Capstone Equities, Rugby Realty, Republic Investment Company acquired building May 2024 for $51.4M.
stories.summary: Conduct AI, a London-based artificial intelligence firm developing enterprise software, has established its first U.S. office by signing a 6,705-square-foot lease on the entire third floor of 140 Crosby Street in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. JLL represented the landlord partnership of Capstone Equities, Rugby Realty, and Republic Investment Company, which acquired the building in May for $51.4 million. Building asking rents range from $150 to $165 per square foot.
stories.impact: International AI and software firms expanding U.S. presence and establishing flagship offices in high-amenity Manhattan neighborhoods (SoHo) signal ongoing tech talent concentration and corporate relocation to NYC. Conduct AI's entry reinforces SoHo's appeal to fast-growing software and AI companies, driving demand for adjacent residential from young, educated tech workers. Developers should prioritize multifamily projects in SoHo, Noho, and East Village with co-working, fitness, and high-speed internet—tech tenants are premium multifamily renters willing to pay for neighborhood walkability and office cluster proximity.
